import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Latin Tableau Conjecture

The Latin Tableau Conjecture states that the graph associated
to any (finite) Young diagram (i.e., whose vertices are the
cells of the diagram, with edges between cells in the same row
or column) is CDS-colorable, meaning that there exists a proper
coloring of the vertices of the graph such that for all k > 0, the
number of vertices with color < k equals the maximum size of
the union of k independent sets of the graph.

*References:*

* [The Latin Tableau Conjecture](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/view/v32i2p48)
-/

namespace LatinTableau

variable {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]

namespace SimpleGraph

/-- The Latin Tableau Conjecture: If G is the simple graph
  of a Young diagram, then G is CDS-colorable. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem LatinTableauConjecture (μ : YoungDiagram) :
     μ.toSimpleGraph.CDSColorable := by sorry

reformulations.difference: Lean asserts CDS-colorability of every Young-diagram graph, using one coloring whose first k color classes attain the maximum union size for every k. The original conjecture characterizes all realizable tableau types by dominance by the chromatic difference sequence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proper colorings of the specified graph are exactly Latin tableaux. Writing α_k for indepNumK G k, the prefix equations give color-class sizes α_(i+1) − α_i. Proposition 3 of the paper says these differences are weakly decreasing for partition graphs, so this realizes precisely the CDS as the tableau type; conversely, a tableau of this type can have its colors relabeled to satisfy the prefix equations. Proposition 5 and Corollary 6 explicitly establish that realizing the CDS for every shape is equivalent to the full conjecture: every dominated type is then realizable, and dominance is necessary by the definition of α_k. The supporting prefix/difference equivalence and the harmless k=0 extension were proved in Lean, but the full equivalence involving dominance was not.

reformulations.difference: The imported definition permits overlapping independent sets, whereas Definition 1 of the source describes a union of k disjoint stable sets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Replace each set S_i by S_i minus the union of its predecessors. The resulting sets remain independent, are pairwise disjoint, and have exactly the same union. Thus the attainable union cardinalities, and hence their maxima, are identical. The iff between the two feasibility predicates and equality of their suprema were proved in the scratch file.

sources_consulted: Chow and Tiefenbruck, “The Latin Tableau Conjecture,” Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 32(2) (2025), #P2.48, article page: https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/view/v32i2p48

Published paper: https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v32i2p48/pdf — especially §§1–2, Definitions 1–2, Propositions 3 and 5, Corollary 6, and the partial results and concluding remarks in §§4–5.
https://arxiv.org/e-print/2408.04086 — downloaded and read the corresponding v1 LaTeX source.
review.notes: Checked the sole theorem and all relevant imported definitions. The research-open tag agrees with the cited paper's partial-results status. Lean experiments proved the exact adjacency characterization, attainment and boundedness of indepNumK on finite graphs, the k=0 case, and CDS-colorability of the empty and single-cell diagrams. A computable enumeration was proved equal to indepNumK and tested on small rows, columns, hooks, and a 2×2 square. Final checks are in /workspace/review/final_checks.lean; the proofs do not depend on sorryAx or the conjecture under review. No repository files were edited.
